name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
problem: Large language models struggle with multi-step arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning, and standard prompting gives the model no room to work through intermediate steps.
mechanism: Not an architecture change: PROMPT with a few chain-of-thought EXEMPLARS in which the worked solution is written out as a series of intermediate reasoning steps, so the model imitates the step-by-step format at inference. Reasoning ability is elicited emergently by scale rather than trained.
speedup_reported: NOT A SPEEDUP PAPER - and the cost implication is the opposite of one. Prompting a 540B-parameter model with EIGHT chain-of-thought exemplars achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on GSM8K, surpassing even FINETUNED GPT-3 WITH A VERIFIER. For this repo the operative consequence is the COST: every intermediate reasoning step is an OUTPUT token, and output tokens are the bandwidth-bound resource that dominates decode latency. CoT is therefore a latency and cost multiplier imposed by the prompt, not a free accuracy win, and this is the origin point for that accounting.
notes: ADOPTION: in-production beyond dispute - chain-of-thought prompting is universal in deployed systems and needs no engine support at all. VENUE: NeurIPS 2022; the arXiv comment field does not state it, so venue rests on the widely-attested NeurIPS 2022 publication and should be re-verified against Semantic Scholar, which was rate-limited at verification time. INCLUDED AS THE COST-ORIGIN RECORD for the inference-time-compute sub-area: every downstream record (s1 budget forcing, self-consistency, best-of-N) multiplies the token count this paper introduced, and the reason reasoning tokens are expensive is precisely that they are output tokens on the memory-bandwidth-bound decode path. Deliberately hardware_relevance = [] because the technique is hardware-independent; the hardware dependence enters only through the token count it creates.
